title: B.C. to pay funeral costs for man shot by police
article: The province has decided to cover the bill to bring the body of a man shot by Vancouver police back home to Prince Rupert.
Gerald Chenery drew a knife and was shot a number of times by two rookie cops in a downtown Vancouver alley on Boxing Day.
"My brother and his wife heard the Ministry of Human Resources gave the go-ahead to have him sent home for burial," said Teresa Chenery, Gerald's sister.
Teresa Chenery, who is on income assistance and supports six children, said she had been told by the ministry that it would not cover bereavement costs.

The ministry said it was delayed in providing necessary support for the family due to difficulty identifying next of kin, which eventually turned out to be Chenery's biological father and not his sister.
"It's unfortunate when process interferes with a grieving situation," said Richard Chambers, the ministry's director of communications.
"It turns out there was a strong case for the ministry helping this family."
As soon as Chenerys father was located, the necessary documents were forwarded to him and the request for assistance was honoured, said Chambers.
This includes transportation and some burial costs.
